effective_resolution_note: classes 1-4 are driven by climate (1-4 km), SOTWIS 1:500 000 map units and 250 m SoilGrids; the 100 m grid is a sampling grid. Class 5 uses vector restrictions at their mapped precision.
confidence_method: Monte-Carlo agreement: share of 24 draws (SoilGrids/SOTWIS/terrain/climate inputs perturbed by documented error models, ML ensemble member and fusion thresholds resampled) that reproduce the central class. It measures robustness to input uncertainty, NOT validated map accuracy.

label_basis.1: rule-derived (FAO-style limiting-factor evaluation) + ML cultivation-likelihood evidence; never field-verified
label_basis.2: rule-derived + ML evidence; includes land observed under cultivation in 2021 (observed, WorldCover+IO LULC)
label_basis.3: rule-derived: reversible/partially reversible severe limitation(s); feasibility NOT assessed here (see Model 2)
label_basis.4: rule-derived: irreversible limitation (steepness, stoniness, hyper-aridity <100 mm/yr, gypsic, temperature) or ML-unsupported

data_sources.name: ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0
data_sources.role: covariate (pH, SOC, texture, CEC, coarse fragments) - ML-predicted soil maps

data_sources.name: SOTWIS Jordan v1.0 (ISRIC)
data_sources.role: covariate (EC, ESP, gypsum, CaCO3, drainage) - legacy 1:500 000 survey units
data_sources.license: CC BY 3.0 per data hub (zip text: non-commercial) - flagged

data_sources.name: Impact Observatory 10 m annual LULC v02

acquisition_date_range.sentinel2: not used by v0.1 checkpoint (see docs/MODEL1_SUITABILITY.md)

mc_error_model: SoilGrids pH/SOC/sand/clay N(mu,(Q95-Q05)/3.29); other SoilGrids lognormal 0.25; SOTWIS lognormal 0.5; slope lognormal 0.15; rainfall lognormal 0.20; temperature N(0,1 degC)
notes: Suitability classes are rule-derived (FAO-style) with ML and observed-cultivation evidence; no field-verified 5-class ground truth exists.
Irrigation water availability (groundwater, licences) is NOT modelled; class 4 in <100 mm/yr land means no rainfed option, not that irrigation is impossible.
Restrictions come from OpenStreetMap/WorldCover and are incomplete; always verify legal status before decisions.

observed_cultivated_without_override.note: classes these cells would get if the observed-cultivation override (class<=2) were switched off; this is the non-circular check

mean_ml_cultivation_probability.note: in-sample for Jordan-wide training (Ma'an cells were in the final training set); the leave-governorate-out numbers are the held-out evidence

agreement_with_observed_cultivation.note_on_circularity: The delivered map caps observed-cultivated cells at class 2 BY DESIGN (observed override), so the high class-2 share of observed_cultivated is partly by construction; see observed_cultivated_without_override for the rule/ML-only view.
agreement_with_observed_cultivation.reading: 99.1% of observed-cultivated cells fall in classes 1-2, 0.9% in classes 3-4, 0.0% in class 5. Labels: WorldCover-2021 AND IO-LULC-2021 cropland agreement at 100 m (land-cover products, not field survey). Class 3/4 membership of observed farms is a limitation: the rules use 1-4 km climate and 1:500,000 soil units and are conservative at farm scale; the 10 ha minimum-mapping-unit sieve also removes small cultivated patches.
